Action Plan:
1. Viral-type upper respiratory tract infection (dry cough, rhinorrhea, myalgias, chills): advise 1–2 days off work, rest, oral fluids, regular paracetamol as required; return for review if no improvement within 2–3 days or if worsening breathlessness/fever; antibiotics may be considered at that point.
2. Alcohol consumption: reduce to ≤2 glasses of wine per week for the next few weeks, then aim for complete cessation to support blood pressure and diabetes control.
3. Chronic disease management (type 2 diabetes, hypertension): continue Metformin and Lisinopril as prescribed; maintain routine primary-care follow-up and home BP/glucose monitoring; reinforce smoking cessation.
4. Safety-net advice reiterated: attend earlier if chest pain, significant dyspnea, or persistent high fever develop.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: 5–6 day history of continuous dry cough (worse at night) and runny nose.  
• Associated symptoms: chills/shivering (subjective fever), generalized myalgias and lethargy; transient diarrhea at illness onset, now resolved; no sputum, chest pain, dyspnea on exertion, sore throat beyond cough irritation, ear pain, nausea, vomiting, urinary symptoms, or rash.  
• Past medical history: type 2 diabetes; hypertension.  
• Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented); Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: none known.  
• Family history: father with type 2 diabetes.  
• Social history: lives with partner; IT developer; ex-smoker (quit 6 months ago); drinks wine 2–3 glasses on ~3 evenings/week.

Objective:
• No physical examination findings or vital signs documented.  
• No investigations performed or reviewed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dry cough and upper respiratory symptoms  
   - Assessment: Viral upper respiratory tract infection.  
   - Differential diagnosis: COVID-19, early bacterial bronchitis (low probability at present).  
   - Investigations planned: none at present.  
   - Treatment planned: rest, adequate hydration, paracetamol as needed; off work 1–2 days; reassess in 2–3 days if no improvement.  
   - Relevant referrals: none at present.

2. Alcohol intake  
   - Assessment: Moderately high alcohol consumption relative to chronic conditions.  
   - Treatment planned: taper to ≤2 glasses/week for several weeks, then trial abstinence.

3. Type 2 diabetes  
   - Assessment: Stable on current therapy (no acute concerns raised).  
   - Treatment planned: continue Metformin; routine monitoring through primary care.

4. Hypertension  
   - Assessment: Stable on current therapy (no acute concerns raised).  
   - Treatment planned: continue Lisinopril; routine BP monitoring; reinforce lifestyle measures (reduced alcohol, smoking cessation maintenance).

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: no documented vitals or physical examination; medication doses/frequencies not recorded.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality acceptable; occasional pauses/over-talk but clinically clear.
